question: In the sodium chlorate droplet experiments, which saturated salt solution set the humidity at which single crystals were most frequent?
expect: sodium bromide: single crystals become more frequent at RH about 59%, which saturated NaBr maintained (LiCl 11%, MgCl2 33%) (Experimental Setup; Results)
rendered:
Based on the information in the documents, the answer can be found in the document "Evaporative Crystallization of Sodium Chlorate Droplets under Controlled Humidity in the Presence of a Static Magnetic Field".

On page 2, it is stated that "Saturated solutions of lithium chloride, magnesium chloride, sodium bromide were employed to maintain the relative humidity in the capped glass container at 11, 33, and 59%, respectively."

On page 4, under the section "Experimental Conditions and Deposition Patterns at RH ≈ 59%", it is stated that "At higher relative humidity (RH ≈ 59%), the fraction of single-crystal deposits increases, indicating that slower evaporation favors crystal growth within the droplet."

Therefore, the saturated solution of sodium bromide set the humidity at which single crystals were most frequent.
